13:- `history/`: every task sent, as its hidden anchor's source, named by the second it was sent and the anchor's name, and beside it, once its run is over, a `.json` record of the same name holding the compiled userPrompt the harness received, the system prompt as it received it and the harness it went to, whether it has been marked done by hand for sending to the other mode, each line the harness printed, each message sent to the task while it ran, in its place among those lines, any error, when the task was sent and when it ended, and beside it the harness's session for its conversation as the run left it, a `.session` folder of the same name, as the [HarnessIntegration](../harness-integration/index.md#harness-integration) says, and when each of its phases began and ended, as the debug log names them, to the millisecond, and, in a git repository, the hashes of the two snapshots of the
14:- `snapshot-index`: in a git repository, the private index the task snapshots are built with, as they say
35:Some of it belongs to one machine rather than to the project: the harness report `.suspense/harness.json`, the fluency `.suspense/fluency.md`, printed by this machine's piton, the Suspense fluency `.suspense/suspense-fluency.md`, written by this machine's Suspense, the queue `.suspense/queue/`, the commit notes `.suspense/commit-notes.json`, the conversations left `.suspense/conversations.json`, whose conversations only this machine's harness knows, the harness's sessions `.suspense/sessions/`, which hold its transcripts, the snapshot index `.suspense/snapshot-index`, and the draft `.suspense-draft.pi` wherever it is, should it ever be written. Git ignores these, so they are never committed. Everything else, the prompt history, the questions, the divergence reports, the system prompts, and the project's Containerfile, is kept with the project.
38:## Task Snapshots
40:In a project that is a git repository, every task the harness runs keeps a record of the files that changed while it ran. When the harness actually starts the task, not when it is sent or queued, the project's working tree is snapshotted, and it is snapshotted again when the run is over, however it ends: done, failed, or cancelled. In a project that isn't a git repository, nothing is snapshotted or recorded, and nothing about it is shown anywhere.
41:A snapshot is a git tree, made with git's plumbing alone: `git add -A` and then `git write-tree`, run with `GIT_INDEX_FILE` pointing at a private index, `.suspense/snapshot-index`, so the repository's own index, HEAD, branches, stash, and working tree are never read from or written to. The private index is kept between snapshots, so each one hashes again only the files whose timestamps changed since the last. A snapshot follows `.gitignore`, as git does, so ignored files, `.suspense`'s machine-only data among them, are never in it. No commit, branch, worktree, or stash is ever made, nothing is added to the user's history, and no tool but git is needed.
42:Both trees are pinned so git's garbage collection never deletes them, each under a private ref, `refs/suspense/<task>/before` and `refs/suspense/<task>/after`, `<task>` being the task's hidden anchor's name, and their hashes are kept in the task's history record. A snapshot that can't be taken, as when git fails, is left out rather than stopping the task; a task missing either snapshot shows no changed files.
43:The private index and the refs belong to this machine: `snapshot-index` is ignored by git like the other machine-only data, and the refs are never pushed, since nothing pushes `refs/suspense/`.
13:A file's status is one of modified, added, untracked, conflicted, or ignored; an unchanged file has none. A renamed file counts as modified. Everything inside an ignored folder is ignored too. A folder takes the most pressing status among its contents, conflicted first, then modified, added, and untracked.
17:Modified is amber, added green, untracked teal, and conflicted red, each a shade readable in both the light and the dark theme. Ignored is dimmed.

content.text:
Task snapshots now cover only the project directory. When the project is a subfolder of a larger repository, files outside it are no longer snapshotted or listed among a task's changed files.

- **Snapshots:** they are still built with `git add -A` against the private index, but now only on the project's own folder. The first snapshot after this change drops any outside files an older snapshot had put in that index.
- **Changed files:** the list is limited to the project folder too. So a task whose first snapshot was taken before this change, while it was still running, doesn't show outside files as deleted.
- **Git status:** this part already worked, so I only added a test for it. `git status --ignored=matching` already reports an ignored folder as one entry (`target/` or `build/`, not every file inside it), and the project tree already dims everything within it.

The new tests pass: one for snapshots in a subfolder project, and a check that an ignored folder is a single entry.

In the full suite, the same 14 tests as before fail because your uncommitted spec rename broke them (`ApplicationScope` is now `Application`). `quitting_while_a_task_runs_asks_first` also failed in the full run but passed twice on its own.
